basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 3.' and it opens 'Vers. 3. Dixit Deus. Non voce carnea, nec motu labiorum, sed dixit, id est, voluit. Velle'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 3. Dixit Deus. Non voce carnea, nec motu labiorum, sed dixit, id est, voluit. Velle enim ejus dicere est. Unde scriptum est: Dixit, et facta sunt (Psalm. CXLVIII, 5). Vel etiam dixit, id est, Filium genuit per quem omnia facta sunt. Fiat lux. Lux dicitur a luendo, id est a purgando tenebras. Lux autem illa non ejusmodi erat quae nunc est sole superposito, sed qualis esse solet vel ante solis ortum, vel post ejus occubitum.
